intent: A grid of cells, rows by columns, like weekday by hour, where each cell's shade shows its value. One hue from light to dark, a low-to-high legend, a tooltip per cell and a table view.
useWhen: When something happens across two dimensions, like runs by weekday and hour or errors by service and day
Spotting busy and quiet patches in a dense grid, where reading every number would be slow
One measure over a fixed set of rows and columns, with gaps that matter
doNotUseWhen: Exact values people compare cell by cell — use Table or DataTable
Editing values in cells — use DataGrid
Dated events people open or change — use Calendar
Change over time for one or a few series — use LineChart
A short ranking by one measure — use BarList

rows.note: Row labels, top to bottom, like Mon to Sun. Each label is unique.

columns.note: Column labels, start to end, like 00 to 23. Each label is unique.

value.note: Zero or more. Shaded against the largest value in data.

data.note: One entry per cell with a value. A cell with no entry shows as empty (No data), a cell with 0 shows as zero; both keep a visible outline. Entries for unknown rows or columns are ignored.

valueFormatter.note: (value: number) => string for the tooltip, the legend ends and the table. Defaults to the chart format: 1,240, 12.4k, 1.2M.

title.note: Chart heading on the frame, like the other charts. Also names the grid for screen readers.

description.note: One line under the title, like the time range.

requirements: Title on the figure when provided, and the grid is named by it
The cells are a role=grid with column and row headers; the grid is one Tab stop and arrow keys, Home and End move between cells
Each cell names its row, column and value (or No data) and shows the tooltip on focus as well as on hover
Shade is never the only cue: the tooltip and the table view give every value as text
The Table toggle swaps the grid for a plain table with every value

doNot: Do not build a heatmap from a Table with coloured cells or from loose divs — use Heatmap
Do not use several hues or status colours for the scale; it is one measure in one hue
Do not use it for exact values people compare cell by cell — use Table
Do not squash the grid on small screens; it scrolls sideways inside its frame
Do not pass negative values; the scale starts at zero
Do not use raw hex or primitive --color-* ramps
snippet:
<Heatmap
  title="Agent runs by hour"
  description="Last 7 days"
  rows={["Mon", "Tue", "Wed"]}
  columns={["09", "10", "11"]}
  data={[
    { row: "Mon", column: "09", value: 12 },
    { row: "Mon", column: "10", value: 30 },
    { row: "Tue", column: "11", value: 4 },
  ]}
/>
